decision_reason: Judge sees only the letter and infers the word, so the pick is judged on the letter's modal inferred word plus copy position, not on a private word. Q (quietly quitting) and U (unhinged) were REJECTED after live validation of comp.json (2,564 entries): 'quietly quitting' already submitted twice plus Q for Quitting/Queasy/Queue, 55 Q titles; 'unhinged' submitted 8+ times, 71 U titles — byte-identical copies share one rate and the earlier receipt places above, so a late Q/U copy is nearly worthless. I wins on: (2) vivid/specific — insomnia is a sharp concrete picture (awake at 3 a.m., ceiling-staring, day wrecked by a night that never ended), not a vague mood; (3) darkly funny and repeatable to a friend; (4) honest report of a real day; (5) I fits insomnia exactly, no sharper I-word exists. Copy risk is among the lowest in the field: only 3 explicit earlier 'I for Insomnia' entries and 13 I title-starts. Anchor risk is low: I is not in the description examples (A/F/Z) and not an obvious pick (E/T/S). Specificity lesson from the one-line family applies: generic loses, the most specific word wins.
